summary: Geshe Tashi Tsering works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1977–1993, Lharampa Geshe), Gyuto Monastery (~1993–1994), and under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. He taught at Kopan Monastery (~1990–1992) and Jamyang Buddhist Centre (1994).

Geshe Tenzin Dhargye specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1980–1995), under Ling Rinpoche, and at Gyume Tantric College (1995). His posts included teaching at Gyume (1995–1996) and directing Tibetzentrum Österreich (2008).
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned Geshe degrees at both Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Agvan Dorzhiev (~1921–1937) and at Drepung Monastery (~1923–1938). He later held posts at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983) and Columbia University (~1962–1972).

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He served as a scholar and faculty member at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, with posts attested in 1991, 2004, and 2014–2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1939–1959) and under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1971).
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin pursued traditional monastic studies under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (1896–1906) and under Manshi Kiyozawa (~1899–1903). At Otani University, he served as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gheorghe Bogdan-Duică worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Jena, Vienna, and the University of Bucharest (~1890–1897). In 1919, he became Professor of Modern Romanian Literature at Babeș-Bolyai University.
Gherardo De Vincentiis worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Giacomo Lignana and held an incaricato post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" in 1878.

Gherardo Gnoli worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Antonino Pagliaro (~1954–1958). He held professorships at Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008).

Ghulam Yazdani worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1903–1905) under C. F. Andrews, Mohammad Ishaq, and Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi. He served as Director of Archaeology for Hyderabad State (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Raniero Gnoli at Naples "L'Orientale" (1977–1981) and at Sapienza University of Rome (1982–1985). She was Associate Professor at Naples "L'Orientale" from 1998 to 2017.

Giacomo Devoto was a linguist who studied at Pavia, Berlin, Basel, and Paris under scholars including Luigi Suali and Antoine Meillet. He held professorships at the universities of Cagliari (1927), Florence (1928, 1939), and Padua (1930).

Giacomo Lignana worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Turin and under Christian Lassen and Friedrich von Spiegel. He held chairs at Naples Federico II (1860–1870), Naples "L'Orientale" (director, 1861), and Sapienza University of Rome (1870).
Gianpaolo Vetturini specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1911–1914), where he later served as lecturer (1929) and assistant professor (1935–1948). He was also a professor at Rissho University.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya and later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1968–1972) and Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998), studying under Carl Bielefeldt, Bernard Faure, and others. He has taught at the Insight Meditation Center (~1990) and Sati Center (~1997).
